articleTitle: Improved Sliding Mode Control Based on Perturb & Observe for Maximum Power Point Tracking from PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper gives a comparison between the maximum power point control algorithms of the Photovoltaic system (PVs) with Perturb & Observe (P&O), Sliding mode control (SMC) and Sliding mode control improved (SMC improved). Since the nonlinear nature of Voltage-Current characteristics is highly dependent on temperature and solar irradiance, therefore, the authors will consider their changes based on possible cases in practice, then compare and choose the best method for PV s. Currently, the authors can use many different methods to improve the most optimal conditions for PVs. Especially, it can be mentioned that the method of changing the surface of the SMC improve algorithm based on P&O algorithm for boost converter, the authors will see high efficiency, high maximum point power, stability, accuracy with fast convergence rate although the weather changes equally according to specific environmental conditions through simulation on the MATLAB SIMULINK.

articleTitle: A Short Review on the Situation of Municipal Biodegradable Solid Waste Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Biodegradable solid waste (BSW) is the main component of municipal solid waste (MSW), accounting for a significant proportion of 44%. Handling BSW varies depending on the situation of the waste management system and socioeconomic conditions of each country. This study aims at giving a short review of the current situation of BSW treatment methods in the World. With the high amount of BSW, landfilling and incineration are the most reliable methods for low- and middle-income countries. While in developed nations, BSW accounted for 20–40% of the total waste, making Waste-to-Energy the second-best option besides recycling. With a low efficiency of waste segregation at source, BSW in Vietnam accounted for 55-75% of the total MSW. Landfilling was the main method of handling BSW in Vietnam, with 76%, followed by composting with 16%, and the remaining 13% was sent to incineration plants. Since 2022, the Vietnamese Government has promulgated the Environmental Protection Strategies, with the main target being to increase waste recycling and reduce the waste to landfill to 30% by 2025. To achieve these goals, further study to enhance the application of sustainable methods for BSW treatment must be focused.

articleTitle: Digital Instrument Keyboard Inspection System Using Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, there are more cases of non-face-to-face activities, and more cases of enjoying hobbies in an indoor independent space. Among electronic musical instruments whose demand has increased, digital pianos are also often used in individual homes. In the case of digital pianos, manual visual inspection is often performed during inspection, so they have a slow production speed. The method proposed in this paper can improve productivity and increase data utilization by automating the inspection process using an inspection system equipped with vision camera, sensor, and cylinder. When a piano is inspected using the system, defects are quickly detected and inspection accuracy is improved, thereby reducing costs and improving productivity. It becomes possible to monitor the process status using big data. Using the proposed method, a 40percent time reduction over manual inspection can be achieved and big data can be placed in a high position.

articleTitle: Investigate the Frequency Effect to the Deformation and Vibration of Amorphous Steel Core Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Magnetostriction force causes vibration and deformation on the steel core of the transformer. The frequency element is also an important parameter causing deformation and vibration in the transformer core. The article has built a mathematical model to investigate the effect of frequency on the deformation of the steel core of amorphous transformers. Simulation results by finite element method on Ansys Maxwell software, the largest core deformation occurs at 560Hz is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17,25\mu \mathfrak{m}/\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The investigate shows that the frequency affecting to the deformation and vibrations of the steel core occurs in the range of 450Hz to 750Hz. In addition, frequency range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\text{Rz}\leq \mathrm{T}\leq 350$</tex> Hz deformation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}} < 7\mu \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{m}$</tex> and vibration is not significant. Determining the frequency and deformation position of the steel core will contribute to perfecting the production process and selecting amorphous steel core transformers to be installed in manufactories. other hand, when installing transformers for factories, it is necessary to measure and analyze harmonics of power source, and always attention to this frequency range to avoid the influence of harmonics causing strong magnetostriction force, breaking structure of the steel core.

articleTitle: Vilayer: Pavement Analysis Program
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The pavement structure is a significant cost component in a road construction project. Furthermore, the pavement structure's quality also impacts a road network's operational capability and service capacity. Therefore, the design of the pavement structure plays a crucial role in enhancing project quality and reducing construction costs. Mechanistic-Empirical Pavement Design (MEPD) are widely employed in road pavement structure design in developed countries. Following this approach, calculating stress, strain, and displacement is paramount. In this study, the pavement analysis program VILAYER is developed and designed to improve user experience. The Burmister theory is applied to compute stress, strain, and displacement along various directions at calculation points within flexible road pavement layers. In addition, the Gaussian quadrature integral technique and the Richardson extrapolation are implemented to improve the accuracy of calculations for points near the surface layer of the flexible pavement structure. The renowned pavement analysis program BISAR is chosen to participate in the verification process of the VILAYER. Moreover, the common flexible pavement structures in Vietnam are used for comparative analysis of stress, strain, and displacement calculations between the VILAYER and BISAR. As a results, there is no significant difference between the two program's computed stress, strain, and displacement values. Thus, the VILAYER program is a promising candidate for the practical application of MEPD method in designing flexible pavement structures in Vietnam.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Free Vibration of Porous Functionally Graded Beams with Different Boundary Conditions and a Novel Two-Variable Model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study introduces a new approach to the vibration analysis of porous functionally graded (PFG) beams by utilizing a two-dimensional elasticity solution. Polynomial and trigonometric series are used to enhance the kinematics of a beam with only two variables along the thickness and axial axes, respectively. The beams' characteristic equations are then derived using Lagrange's equations. Material characteristics, porosity, and boundary conditions all have an effect on natural frequencies, which is explored in this parametric study.

articleTitle: Determining Cable Tensile Loads Considering Viscous Damping
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Recently., determining the tensile load in the structures with cable., such as suspension bridges and cable-stayed bridges., is an important problem. This structure could be ensured to be durable by structural health monitoring., including structural inspections and patrol measurements. A part of the inspection methods is vibration monitoring; nevertheless., this could be inaccurate because geometry and material characteristics are directly influent., such as cable's material damping and the sag. This research on the dynamic differential equations of vibration cable., which is taken to determine the tensile loads of cables., considers the viscous damping of cable material. After that., the assumption of this research would be simplified boundary conditions. The relation between frequencies and tensile load is obtained by expressions. A practical mechanics model., which is proposed., is used to determine the tensile load of the cables through measured frequency. This model is performed to apply for four cables of a cable-stayed road bridge across the Saigon River in Ho Chi Minh City.

articleTitle: Performance of a Prosthetic Arm Using Mindwave Neurosky Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Brain Computer Interfaces (BCI) are technologies that enable the execution of actions on a computer based on brainwaves. Brainwaves are recorded using electroencephalography (EEG) to facilitate computer processing. In this study, the Neurosky Mindwave device was employed as the input signal for brainwave-controlled manipulation of a 3D-printed prosthetic arm, constructed and assembled using adult human arm proportions and structure. The device captures electrical signals through sensors and measures various brainwave types, including Gamma, Delta, Theta, Alpha, and Beta waves. This device wirelessly transmits data to a personal computer (PC) via Bluetooth. Consequently, the acquired signals can be processed and classified into motion categories using MATLAB's graphical user interface (GUI). The classified data is then forwarded to an Arduino Uno, which controls the robotic arm's motors. System testing demonstrated the potential to employ human brainwaves for performing fundamental motions with the prosthetic arm, achieving a success rate of up to 90% following training. The average success rate, determined to be nearly 80% during the experimentation, indicates that the Neurosky Mindwave device holds promise as a viable option for the development of such prosthetic devices.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Hardened Properties of Green Mortar Produced with the Blends of GGBFS and Waste Red Brick Powder Based on Alkali-Activated Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study investigates the hardened properties of mortar specimens produced by alkali-activated materials with ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) blended with waste red brick powder (WRBP). Three mixtures containing 40% red brick powder with water-to-solid ratios (w/s) of 0.35, 0.4 and 0.5 were designed, accompanied by a non-WRBP mixture with w/s of 0.4. The hardened properties were examined via compressive strength, ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV), length change, and electrical surface resistivity (ESR) up to 28-day of curing age. The results illustrated that reusing WRBP slightly reduced the mechanical properties of mortar samples. Besides, increasing w/s ratio significantly mitigated the engineering properties of the specimens. At 28-day, the green mortar samples exhibited a good quality with high UPV values (>3660m/s), ESR values <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(> 20\mathrm{k}\Omega-\text{cm})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Latent Structure of Risks in Transportation Projects in Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In transportation projects, effective risk management significantly impacts critical elements such as cost, scheduling, quality, and stakeholder relationship. Reality shows that transportation projects in Vietnam have encountered risks that affects project success, leading to the need for risk control measures, especially within construction phase. This study conducts a questionnaire survey to investigate the perception of stakeholders on risks in construction phase in transportation projects in Vietnam. Factor analysis was conducted based on a list of 25 risks compiled from relevant publications. This study employed exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to explore latent risk structures in transportation projects, identifying four main risk groups: “supervision risks”, “changes and stakeholder risks”, “environmental risks” and “construction risks”, each comprising various component risks. This empirical insight provides valuable guidance to practitioners and policymakers involved in project execution, enhancing their decision-making efficacy, thus, improving the projects efficiency.

articleTitle: Applying Tools of Lean – Six Sigma Method in the Plastic Products Industry: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study aims to provide an overview of the problems, the causes that occur, and some suitable solutions as planning the maintenance time of the screws holding the bellows holder in the extrusion stage, creating a standardized for spray manipulation in the extrusion stage, re-layout the inventory, creating the visual management of the defect control process to reduce waste, prevent and minimize the risks of the defective product and help workers conduct task quickly and efficiently by applying the DMAIC model (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control) with supported tools such as Seven wastes, Cause and effect diagram, Pareto chart, 5S, Visual management. Further, a case study on the Plastic Company is discussed, emphasizing the production process area. The result obtained was that the time for searching measuring instruments during production was reduced by 95.8%, the maximum material capacity in the warehouse increased by 13.8%, the aisle area in the warehouse increased by 19.6%, time taken by staff to get materials from the warehouse decreased by 2.27%.

articleTitle: Study the Effect of Casting Parameters on Mechanical Properties of Aluminum Products Producing in Metal Injection Molding
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research investigates the influence of casting parameters on the mechanical properties of high-pressure die-cast aluminum alloy ADC12 products. Initially, the high-pressure die-casting (HPDC) process was simulated using software. Subsequently, the products were cast using the YOTA DC 100V5 machine. The microstructure of the products was examined under an optical microscope, followed by hardness testing using the Rockwell scale. The experimental results indicate that an increase in the first-phase distance leads to a decrease in hardness, while raising the accumulator pressure can enhance the hardness.

articleTitle: Multi-Classification Protocol for Building Electricity Consumption Modelling Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The growing demand for energy in developed and developing countries has made it necessary to evaluate energy use to conserve energy. Many studies have been conducted to understand the energy use of appliances in buildings. Effective energy management and accurate forecasting of building energy consumption have become essential factors in investment decision-making and increasing the market value of construction projects. This study proposes an ANN multi-classification to optimize energy use in buildings using real data. By using Sobol indices with Ishigami function for assigning weights to input variables, we show their importance relation support to train ANN model. Furthermore, the study results serve as reference data for engineers and managers in the design and management of buildings.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Surface Quality on the Bending Fatigue Strength of Wire Arc Additive Manufactured Carbon Steel
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study delves into the intricate relationship between surface quality, microstructural characteristics, mechanical properties, and fatigue strength of wire arc additive manufactured (WAAM) carbon steel. Firstly, the WAAM-printed components demonstrated remarkable consistency in wall thickness, with a minor variation ranging from 3.6 mm to 4.2 mm and an average thickness of approximately 3.95 mm. Crucially, no discernible pores or significant printing defects were observed, affirming the robustness and effectiveness of the printing process for high-quality outcomes. Microstructure analysis revealed the presence of equiaxed ferrite grains predominantly composed of iron, supplemented with minor carbon and alloying elements. This unique microstructural arrangement endowed the material with excellent ductility and formability, making it suitable for various fabrication processes. Hardness assessments displayed uniformity, with an average hardness of approximately 158 HV observed across the entire WAAM-processed component, emphasizing material property consistency. Surface roughness assessments, encompassing Ra and Rz values, exposed significant variations among different surface treatments. The polished sample boasted superior surface quality with an Ra value of 0.32 um, while the machined sample exhibited slightly higher roughness at 1.71 um, Conversely, the as-built surface displayed pronounced roughness, registering an Ra value of 20.67 um, These findings suggested potential implications for fatigue strength, with the as-built sample anticipated to exhibit compromised fatigue resistance. Tensile tests unveiled impressive mechanical properties, with a maximum tensile strength of 499 MPa, a yield strength of 379 MPa, and a notable elongation of 39%. However, these strengths were relatively lower than those of the welding wire, attributed to variations in heat input between the WAAM process and traditional welding techniques. Bending fatigue tests examined the fatigue limits of the samples, with the machined sample demonstrating a fatigue limit of 250 MPa, and surprisingly, the polished sample exhibiting a slightly lower limit at 200 MPa. Further investigation revealed that the polished sample harbored residual tensile stresses induced by the electropolishing process, negatively affecting its fatigue strength. In contrast, the as-built sample displayed the lowest fatigue strength at approximately 130 MPa, attributed to its inferior surface quality and heightened susceptibility to crack initiation.

articleTitle: Effect of Short Piles Strengthened in Sand Leveling Over Soft Soils Using 2D Physical Model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper studies the efficacy of short piles on soft ground with sand leveling, using a 2D physical model. The study focuses on the geological characteristics of the Mekong Delta, characterized by a substantial layer of soft soil overlaying a 2 ÷ 5m thick stratum of leveling sand. The small (i.e., cross-section is smaller than 30×30 cm) and short piles (i.e., pile length is shorter than 5 m) could be selected for low-rise buildings in such soil conditions. 18 physical models were conducted in this study. The Schneebeli analogue material, foam, and steel bars with square cross sections were used to simulate the sandy, clayey layers and short reinforced concrete piles, respectively. Vertical loading tests were executed on groups of 3 piles, with variable parameters including pile spacing (S), and the distance from the pile tip to the boundary between the two soil layers (H). The results show that under constant S and decreasing H, the deformation beneath the pile tip diminishes. Conversely, under constant S and decreasing H, the deformation beneath the pile tip diminishes. Using a raft increases not only the bearing capacity of the piles but also the deformation in the vertical direction. On the contrary, the deformation expands horizontally in the case of pile groups.

articleTitle: Application of SLP And LEAN Method in Designing the Layout of Auto Parts Manufacturing Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In the current Vietnamese market, the demand for automobiles is increasing, leading to the development of the auto parts manufacturing industry. VPIC (Vietnam Precision Industry Company) is a Vietnamese auto parts factory. Surveying VPIC, the team found that waste still exists on the production floor and production efficiency is not optimal. Therefore, in this study, the team will practice the layout of production facilities for a specific product code. Applying the SLP method, the team will devise a plan to minimize transportation costs, increase the connection between areas, and minimize the distance to move materials. In addition, the implementation combined with the Lean method to build a lean production system, thereby increasing the operational efficiency of the auto parts factory. The project successfully used FlexSim software to evaluate and select an optimal layout model for the material movement, along with suggestions on applying Lean for the purpose of production moderation. However, the topic still has the problem of the number of WIPs between the CNC Turning and Welding stages because the production time is much different. To solve this problem, the team proposed implementing production scheduling and dispatching to make the material flow more fluid, which would help businesses optimize resources and increase production efficiency.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Color Variation of Cotton Fabric Dyed with Coffee Grounds Through Color Space and Color Histogram
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This work focused on evaluating color variation of cotton fabrics dyed with extracts from coffee grounds under effects of brewing ratio (1:5, 1:10, 1:20 and 1:40), additional (2nd) dyeing time, mordanting agents (ferrous sulfate: FE, kali alum: KA, natural tannin: TN) and washing condition. According to color space of CIE Lab and color histogram obtained from a spectrophotometer and digital photos, color difference (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\text{ELab}$</tex>) was revealed. The experimental results showed that change in brewing ratio moved significantly color coordinates of dyed sample in terms of CIE Lab system. Especially, mordanting agents also caused a great change of colors in image histogram where curves of luminosity, red color, green color and blue colors were shifted. Particularly, dyed samples mordanted with ferrous sulfate (SPFE) were drifted to left (darkness) and dyed samples mordanted with natural tannin (SPTN) were drifted to right (lightness). Furthermore, additional dyed procedures were supposed to highly improve dyeing efficiency for SPFE with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\text{ELab}$</tex> of 8.1441. Finally, color fastness to washing for colored samples with various mordants were experimented with better color retention of SPTN

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Radio Over Fiber for Fronthaul Connection of High-Speed C-RAN
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Radio over Fiber (RoF) is an exotic technology for next-generation wireless networks, including fifth-generation Cloud-Radio Access Networks (C-RAN). In this paper, we propose a fronthaul interface, demonstrated through numerical simulations, for two wireless signal channels in the VHF frequency band using DPSK and CPFSK modulation schemes without needing to use forward error correction coding over a standard single-mode optical fiber span of 20 km. The proposed method is capable of efficiently supporting a high bandwidth of the optical fiber link up to 2.8 Gbps while maintaining a bit error rate (BER) less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup>. Performance analysises have been demonstrated by the numerical simulation for the proposed digital RoF technique. Notably, the performance evaluation of two channels with two advanced digital modulation methods is reported through the analysis of quality parameters, including eye diagrams and signal-to-noise ratio. It is indicated that digital optical links can support long-distance transmission of over 20 km with low-level power laser transmitters without the need for the dispersion compensation process, meeting the requirements of wideband C-RAN systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Convolutional Neural Network Architectures with Long Short-Term Memory for Improved Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In recent years, the application of artificial intelligence and deep learning has expanded to address a variety of tasks, including image classification. Researchers have de-veloped more complex network architectures with more pa-rameters to improve the convergence performance of neural networks. However, this has also increased the complexity of problem-solving and hardware requirements. To address this issue, we propose integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) into known Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures to enhance their performance without significantly increasing complexity. Our experiments with several well-known neural network architectures, including some network architectures such as ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet, evaluated on different datasets such as 525 bird species, CIFAR10, and GTSRB for classification, demonstrate that the integration of LSTM into known CNN architectures can improve their performance in image classification tasks.

articleTitle: A Study of Characteristics of the Mortar Produced from Waste Ceramic as a Fine Aggregate Replacement
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the strength development of mortar samples using waste ceramic (WCS) as a fine aggregate. The WCS was used as a partial replacement for river sand at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% for mortar production. The water-to-binder ratio was fixed at 0.4 and the fly ash (FA) was used at 15% of binder weight. The fresh properties of mortar samples were examined by flowability and fresh unit weight, while the compressive strength and electrical surface resistivity (ESR) of mortar specimens were evaluated up to 28 days of curing age. The influence of aggregate phases on the strength development of mortar samples was investigated with dry and saturated aggregate conditions during the mixing process. The testing results illustrated a reduction in flowability and fresh unit weight by using WCS to river sand. Besides, the compressive strength and ESR values also decreased with increasing WCS content. Using the saturated aggregate phase to produce the mortar samples presented a higher compressive strength than using the dry aggregate phase.

articleTitle: Worker Action Recognition in High Density Conditions based on Edge Device – Cloud Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Construction managers face increasing workloads and time-consuming activities. However, there has been limited application of modern technology like deep learning to improve efficiency on construction sites. This paper focuses on the capabilities of plain vision using YOLO, StrongSORT, 3D CNN, pose estimation and machine learning models for detecting, tracking, and recognizing worker actions. Emphasis is placed on model accuracy for dense and diverse objects per frame, along with proposed solutions for improved YOLO results. Additionally, an adaptable application is developed using a cloud-edge device model, comprising AI and user management parts, to handle high AI workloads in rapidly changing construction environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Current and Electromagnetic Force Acting on Winding in Cases of Short Circuits of Amorphous Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The paper has used the Finite Element Method (FEM) by Ansys Maxwell software to simulate the working modes of amorphous transformers (ATs) with capacity of 1000kVA, voltage 22/0.4kV. The results for rated voltage, no load and full load current are displayed. At the same time, these results are compared with the assessment with preliminary calculations with the aim of confirming the accuracy of the model using the FEM. The paper continues, performing simulations in single-phase, two-phase and three-phase short-circuit fault modes which are very difficult to do in experimental methods. The research has determined the maximum short-circuit current, the short-circuit voltage on the phases of the low voltage (LV) winding. From there, the maximum axial and radial electromagnetic force distribution acting on the phases of the high voltage (HV) and LV windings can be determined. The results show that the maximum short-circuit current of one phase, two phases or three phases combined with the magnetic field in the winding will produce a large electromagnetic force acting on the winding. The results of this research are intended to protect short circuits during transformer operation, which is to serve the adjustment of protective relays. For manufacturing design, based on that we can properly increase the insulation distances or fix the winding position more securely. Since then, this result helps to increase the life of the ATs.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation and Experimentation of the Management of the Charging-Discharging Process of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Currently, with the rapid development of Electric Vehicles (EVs) and electronic devices using Lithium-ion batteries, ensuring stable battery operation and increasing longevity are essential to address economic and environmental concerns. Many research studies have focused on charging and discharging processes with control parameters such as State of Charge (SoC), State of Health (SoH), Temperature, and more. In this article, the authors utilized MATLAB Simulink simulation software in combination with experiments to control the charging and discharging processes based on SoC. The primary objective was to monitor each individual cell within a battery package during charging and discharging to understand the performance variations of lithium-ion batteries during operation.

articleTitle: Modeling Wall Deformation During the Construction of Metro Line 1 (Ho Chi Minh City) Using an Inferred Soil Modulus Derived from SPT Values
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The objective of this study is to assess the deformation of retaining walls during excavations using 2D finite element analysis within the context of the Ho Chi Minh Metro project. The investigation focuses on Opera House station, which is located in a densely populated area near historical buildings and serves as the deepest underground station on Ho Chi Minh City's first metro line. Soil properties are determined based on data obtained from site surveys, in-situ tests, and laboratory experiments. The Hardening Soil Model is applied in numerical simulations to estimate soil stiffness modulus parameters, utilizing results from the Standard Penetration Test (SPT). The results of the 2D finite element analysis, coupled with on-site monitoring, demonstrate that employing the proposed correlation between soil stiffness modulus and SPT index yields accurate simulation results. These results can be valuable for predicting retaining wall displacements in similar excavation projects.

Author Keywords: soil stiffness modulus from SPT test

articleTitle: Kinetic Analysis Of Vietnamese People's Gait
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The discipline of gait analysis plays a crucial role in the evaluation of human health issues and the provision of timely alerts. This research utilizes Kinect cameras to comprehensively monitor and assess human gait. Multiple characteristics pertaining to the movement of the human body throughout the gait cycle are documented. This investigation underscores the significance of gait as a basic element of the human physique, with considerable potential for evaluating health and diagnosing conditions pertaining to essential bodily processes. The present study makes a substantial contribution to enhancing the diagnostic skills and treatment of gait-related issues in the domains of healthcare and human cognition research.

articleTitle: Sprouting Buds of Petunia Hybrida Cuttings Under Normal Conditions in Vitro Culture
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Petunia hybrida is a genus of flowering plants with beautiful colors, popularly grown in modern architecture. In Vietnam, Petunia hybrid is propagated using cuttings or grown from seeds. The application of tissue culture in agriculture produces high-quality and inexpensive plant varieties. In vitro regeneration is a modern and useful method in agriculture. Our research aims to investigate the best sterilization method for samples and the effects of sucrose concentration and coconut water ratio added into Knudson C medium (KC) for sprouting in vitro sprouts of Petunia cuttings under normal conditions. We used a combination of 70%, 75%, and 80% ethanol and 0.5%, 0.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 1% NaOCI to sterilize the samples and studied the effects of sucrose and coconut water added to KC medium on the development of in vitro sprouts. We found that using 70% ethanol combined with 0.75% NaOCI, and then adding 10% (g/L) sucrose and 15% (v/v) coconut water to KC medium ensured the best survival and development of in vitro Petunia hybrida sprouts under normal conditions.

articleTitle: Estimation of Hydrodynamic Forces Acting on the Circular Cable Laying Ship
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Undersea cables layingship are widely used for many purposes such as fishing. It is necessary to evaluate the hydrodynamic forces acting on the cable to ensure the design purposes. This paper presents the estimation of hydrodynamic forces acting on a circular cable attached to a surface ship based on the Reynolds-averaged Navier Stokes approach in Ansys Fluent. The cable is divided into segments and hydrodynamic effect on each segment is calculated for the range of inclined angle from 0 to 90 degrees. The tangential force and normal force acting on the cable segment are calculated for different inclined angles at different speeds. It is verified that the drag coefficients of the cable segment are consistent with the experimental data. The maximum tangential force occurs at an inclined angle of about 40 degrees and the normal force reaches its maximum value in the case of an inclined angle of 90 degrees. The local maximum of normal force appears at an inclined angle of 50 degrees. In addition, the flow pattern over the cable at different inclined angles is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on Reducing Aerodynamic Drag of the Ahmed Model Using the Passive Flow Control Method
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Research using a combined computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation method with the SST <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}-\omega$</tex> turbulence model to passive flow control for reducing aerodynamic drag on the basic Ahmed model 25° (case 1). Passive flow control is achieved by implementing rear air vent holes at the juncture between the rear and side surfaces of the Ahmed model. Three different vent hole cases are created: case 2: 3 holes with a diameter of 20mm, evenly spaced at 60mm intervals; case 3: 3 holes with a diameter of 40mm, evenly spaced at 60mm intervals; case 4: 6 holes with a diameter of 20mm, evenly spaced at 30mm intervals. The simulation results reveal that the vent holes effectively alter the flow of the Ahmed car model, leading to reductions in the aerodynamic drag coefficients by 1.22%, 3.26%, and 2.44% for cases 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Large vent hole diameters yield more significant improvements in reducing aerodynamic drag. However, this may also somewhat compromise the original design of the Ahmed model.

articleTitle: Oil Sorption Application of Anti-Wetting Wax-Coated Loofah Sponged Derived from Nature
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study introduces PW-PW-LS, a hydrophobic material made through a 2-step dipping and spraying process. PW-PW-LS has exceptional potential for environmental use, quickly absorbing floating oil upon contact, with an adsorption capacity of 2.1 to 6.4 times its weight for various oils and solvents. Stability tests show resilience to harsh conditions, including acidic, alkalinity, and salinity, while keeping effectiveness after 20 abrasion cycles. Moreover, PW-PW-LS is biodegradable, enhancing its eco-friendly profile. These findings highlight its practical application in mitigating oil spills and eliminating organic pollutants from water surfaces, aligning with environmental protection and sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition System to Suggest and Respond to Vietnamese Using PhoBert Model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The article proposes an emotion recognition system to suggest and automatically respond in conversations to increase user experience and give immediate feedback. We propose to build an emotion recognition system including six types of emotions (disgust, pleasure, sad, fear, anger, and others) using the PhoBERT model. Besides, we use the dataset built in the article [1] to compare and demonstrate the improvement from the proposal model. The input data is text. The output is the emotional label corresponding to the input. The system has an accuracy of up to 99.8% with the training dataset and 96.4% with the testing dataset. This result is an improvement 15% comparedto [1] showing that we can build a more accurate emotion recognition system for users and be applicable in practice.

articleTitle: Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Servo Control System Design Based On Sliding Mode Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposes a sliding mode controller for regulating the speed of a surface-mounted permanent-magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM). This controller is built by combining the terms of some linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) and mitigates the chattering phenomenon effectively. Moreover, a second-order load torque observer is presented to show the disturbance rejection capability of the proposed method. Finally, the stability of the proposed controller is analytically proven. This paper presents the novel application of LMIs to address the nonlinear control problem, effectively demonstrating the stability of the proposed combined controller. The control algorithm is implemented by using the Matlab/Simulink software. The simulation results are represented to verify the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Desirability Function-Based Robust Design Optimization for Led Lens Design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to propose a multi-objective robust design optimization model based on the desirability functions for LED lens design. Two optical quality characteristics of LED lens design are the viewing angle and luminance uniformity. Based on the experimental design data, the response surface methodology is used to determine the functional relationship between input and output factors. Moreover, the desirability functions are developed to consider the trade-off between two conflicting objectives. Then, two case studies are conducted to verify the efficiency of the proposed methods. The final results imply that the proposed multi-objective robust design optimization model is far more effective than the existing methods in LED lens design.

articleTitle: Severe Shot Peening of PBF-LB Manufactured and Reference 316L – Fatigue Performance and Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study explores the findings concerning the impact of severe shot peening (SSP) on 316L stainless steel, both in laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) and traditional manufacturing routes. Microstructural changes induced by SSP are examined through electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis. The study demonstrates that SSP treatment leads to grain refinement in both materials, but martensitic transformation was only observed in sheet metal. Mechanical testing revealed significant increases in yield strength and ultimate tensile strength in SSP-treated 316L, and fatigue testing under axial and bending loading conditions showed substantial improvements in fatigue limits, with the PBF-LB material benefiting more from SSP treatment. These findings highlight the potential of SSP for enhancing the mechanical properties of 316L stainless steel, making it valuable for applications demanding superior strength and fatigue resistance.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Ship Maneuvering in Regular Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: A key strategy for guaranteeing the ship navigates safely in waves is to improve maneuverability during the design phase. The prediction of ship maneuvering in regular waves is the main topic of this paper. Two distinct approaches are put forth to integrate seakeeping and maneuvering to estimate ship motions in regular waves. First, zero-frequency maneuvering motion and high-frequency wave-induced motion were included in the two-time scale method, which split the fundamental motion equation into two categories. Because the mean second-order wave drift forces affect the maneuvering motion. In this paper, the mean second-order wave drift forces and moments have been estimated using ANSYS-AQWA. Second, the maneuvering force and the nonlinear wave drift force have been added to the unified theory, which uses the retardation function. The retardation function has the advantage of being able to consider additional nonlinear wave loads. Finally, the S175 container ship's standard maneuvering is carried out in regular waves at different wavelengths and is compared to the Free Running Model Test (FRMT) results. The impact of wave direction and wavelength on the ship's drifting distance in regular waves is examined.

articleTitle: Analyze and Evaluate the Factors Affecting the Thermal Comfort Index in the Air-Conditioned Room by Numerical Simulation Software
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Air conditioning systems are becoming more popular than ever in the modern day. They appear all over office buildings, commercial centers, hospitals, etc. With its benefits, people can feel comfortable and comfortable in the space where they work and live. Since then, the research on thermal comfort for people in the air-conditioned room has been focused. CFD simulation is considered one of the scientific research methods related to the flow characteristics of fluids with high applicability. It is an effective tool to understand and evaluate the factors affecting the flow rate. The air-conditioned space's temperature field and velocity will provide the optimal solution for human purposes. The thermal comfort (TC) index was investigated by changing the openings of the cassette air conditioner airflow wide angle (AFWA) to 30°, 40°, 50°, and 60°, respectively, and keeping the ventilation airflow at 400 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>jh fixed. The TC index is surveyed through the Vertical Air Temperature Difference (VATD) index. In addition, the airflow rate of the cassette changed from 810 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>jh to 1230 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>jh during the simulation, thereby giving detailed evaluation results on the indicators affecting thermal comfort inside the room. Using CFD numerical simulation software (Ansys Fluent) to analyze and evaluate the research results shows that changing the AFWA of the air supply significantly when the AFWA increases will affect the uniformity of the comfort index. The AFWA of the louvers gave the highest uniformity and comfort index in this study at 30 degrees and 40° with the ventilation flow value of 810 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>jh at the vertical temperature gradient, VATD has the smallest difference values of 0.95K and 1K, respectively.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Pose Estimation and Action Prediction for Construction Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Monitoring construction sites is an important task to track progress. Here, the assessment of the behavior of construction machines is crucial for this work. In this paper, we present a deep learning-based system to monitor the activity of excavators and wheel loaders – two common construction machines. Our system uses a pose estimation model (YOLO-Pose-based) to obtain their pose, which is then fed into a behavior prediction model (LSTM-based) to assess their working status. We build our own dataset, customize the model, train, and perform the system on the GPU Tesla T4 (Google Colab). Our system achieves mAP 0.927 on our own test set split from our dataset, top 1 & 2 accuracy for action classification are better than 0.9 and real-time speed on video (average at 47.53 FPS) regardless of the number of objects and classes. These results show that our system can be applied to real-world applications.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Vietnamese Braille Printer for Visual Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The Braille printer is a revolutionary assistive technology designed to efficiently cater to the needs of the visually impaired. It converts digital text and graphics into embossed Braille, granting easy access to printed materials. With advanced features like high-quality embossing, user-friendly interfaces, seamless connectivity, and support for tactile graphics, this state-of-the-art Braille printer significantly improves the quality of life and opportunities for visually impaired individuals. This paper presents a simple, low-cost, and easy-to-operate Braille printer, developed through a comprehensive review of relevant literature and an exploration of its design and development process. The printer head is constructed using an Electromagnet mechanism, the movements of the printer axis are driven by the stepper motors, and the main processing unit is an Arduino board. The printer's performance is appraised through expert opinion in the field of Braille text.

articleTitle: A Method of Snoring Symptoms Monitoring in People Helps Diagnose Related Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Frequent snoring state has relation to several health problems including stroke, cardiovascular diseases, overweight and obesity, headaches, sleep apnea, etc. Nowadays, most medical facilities in Vietnam uses polysomnography machine to record people's snoring while sleeping. However, this equipment is quite expensive and must be imported from abroad. This article presents a method for monitoring snoring in humans that aids in diagnosing related diseases. Specifically, we researched the design of a module to record people's snoring sounds while sleeping. The data is stored in the memory card and can also be passed to one or some mobile equipment such as smartphones or laptops via Wi-Fi communication. Doctors can rely on recorded data to analyze and draw relevant diagnostic conclusions. The module is designed to be simple, not bulky, easy to use, and easy to carry or wear on the body.

articleTitle: A Study on Design and Fabrication of a Wave Maker in Laboratory Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposes the prototype of a wave maker for Laboratory Environment. The conceptual design is presented to describe the working principle of the proposed wave maker. Here, a slider crank mechanism is employed to converts continuous rotary motion of a disc into harmonic reciprocating motion on the vertical axis. A curved plate fixed to the end of the crank is forced to move up and down directions. Then, the curved metal force water surface to move forward and backward direction. These motions create the wave form. Moreover, the wave with different amplitude and frequencies is made by changing the crank position and angular velocity of the electric motor. The disc has predrilled hole in some specific positions, so that the end of the crank could be fixed in different position for the distinct waves. A servo motor is employed to change the frequency of the actuator. Finally, an ultrasonic sensor is utilized as an output data in order to verify the water level and wave height. The generated waves can be applied to study in the Laboratory environment.

articleTitle: A Novel Robust Dynamic Surface Control Scheme for Multi-Motor Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: To deal with the nonlinearities, multi-input multi-output, and uncertainties characteristics of multi-motor systems, we propose a robust controller in this paper. A dynamic surface control scheme is designed by taking advantage of backstepping technique, sliding mode control theory, and low-pass filters. In addition, the control structure is also integrated with an observer to estimate moments of inertia which is difficult to measure accurately. By Lyapunov stability and compared simulation results, we prove the stability of the whole system and the control efficiency. As a result, the output response of multi-motor systems demonstrates that the proposed controller improves significantly control quality of the system under time-varying moment of inertia uncertainties.

articleTitle: Economic and Technical Analysis of Hybrid Photovoltaic-Wind Energy Connected to Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This article presents a method for analyzing the economic and technical aspects of hybrid photovoltaic and wind energy systems in the 63 provinces of Vietnam. The study utilizes HOMER PRO software to conduct an economic and technical analysis of a hybrid system designed to meet the standard electricity demand of a household. Based on the analysis results, the installed capacity for the system is determined to be 5 kW of solar photovoltaic panels combined with 1 kW of wind power, resulting in electricity generation ranging from 7932 kWh/year to 9.662 kWh/year. The corresponding levelized cost of electricity (COE) ranges from 0.031 to 0.043 (USD/kWh).

articleTitle: Study of Tetracycline Adsorption on ZIF-8 Under Different Mophologies
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Fast and green synthesis of ZIF-8 (zeolite imidazole framework) and its modifications are reported in two ways: TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>@ZIF-8 and creating mesoporous. The samples were tested by some physic technology such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Infrared Spectroscopy meter (FTIR), and nitrogen adsorption measurements. The results showed clearly the mesoporous and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>@ZIF-8 found in polyhedral morphology. The adsoprtion of Tetracycline (TC) was thoroughly carried out by these hybrids ZIF-8, which showed high adsorption. For the first time, the number of molecules of TC adsorbed outer ZIF-8 surface area and inside its structure was calculated carefully. In general, the study performs a biocompatible synthesis of mesoporous and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>@ZIF-8, successfully applying for TC removal in solution.

articleTitle: Statistical Study on Data Dependency of Memristor Crossbar Architectures for Neuromorphic Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this work, we statistically present the data density dependency of the two memristor crossbar structures, namely the complementary crossbar architecture and the twin crossbar architecture, for neuromorphic image recognition. The two structures perform the Exclusive-NOR computing to find the similarity score between the input vector and the memristor arrays, and both employ the Winner-take-all circuit to determine the winning current. When considering the power consumption, the twin crossbar architecture has proven to consume less energy than complementary crossbar architecture. However, by analyzing the mathematical model of the circuit, we figured out the reduction of output currents as the input image has low density. The observation was verified by the simulation with the data densities of 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, and 0.2. When the data density decreases to low level of 0.2, the maximum current of columns yielding by the twin crossbar architecture decreases about 80% compared to the complementary structure. The Winner-take-all circuit could operate incorrectly under this significant reduction and it could degrade the performance of the twin crossbar architecture. In contrast, twin crossbar architecture can save more power consumption with low-density data. When the density of data is of low of 0.2, the power consumption of the twin crossbar architecture reduces by around 79% in comparison with the complementary structure. These results prove that although being affected by the low-density of data, the twin crossbar architecture has an advantage of low power consumption when working on low-density datasets compared to the complementary crossbar architecture.

articleTitle: The Watershed Planning Methods Affecting the Porous Structural Model for Danang's Coastline in the New Context - Vision to 2045
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The tourist city of Da Nang will become even more livable when harsh weather conditions and natural disasters are minimized to as good as possible. For a city with high porosity to natural conditions, cultural tourism, socio-economic factors, infrastructure, and landscape architecture, such as Da Nang, adverse weather has had a significant impact on watershed planning solutions in urban design for tourism purposes in Da Nang. Watershed planning plays the most crucial role among the factors contributing to the formation of urban sprawl.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Investigations for Aerodynamic Drag Reduction of a Truck Model Using Synthetic Jets
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The oil crisis and climate change represent a challenge for reducing fuel consumption and gas emissions of ground vehicles. This leads to a rapid increase in the number of studies on reducing aerodynamic drag for those vehicles. In this paper, an active flow control method using synthetic jet actuators was applied at the base surface of a scaled-model truck to evaluate their ability of aerodynamic drag reduction. Numerical and experimental studies were conducted. The results presented an aerodynamic drag reduction of 9.82% obtained using synthetic jet devices. Detailed analyses also showed that the application of these devices improves the aerodynamic characteristics of the truck model, reducing the size of the wake region behind the vehicle and increasing the pressure recovery in this area.

articleTitle: Variation of Compressive and Flexural Strength of High-Performance Fine-Grained Concrete within its Components: Some Experimental Results
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: High-performance fine-grained concrete (HPFGC) is increasingly widely used thanks to its ability to respond to the properties of fresh concrete during construction, technical properties, and can be effectively applied in highly aesthetic and slender structures. This paper presents the experimental research results of workability, compressive strength, flexural strength, and porosity of 12 high-performance fine-grained concrete (HPFGCs) using a combination of cement (C), fly ash (FA), ground granulated blast furnace slag (SL), silica fume (SF) with water/binder (w/b) ratio of 0.18. Types of HPFGC are divided into three binder combinations: C-FA-SL, C-FA-SF, C-SL-SF. The results show that: HPGFC with C-FA-SL binder combination increases workability, reduce strength and porosity when increasing the rate of using FA to replace C; HPGFC with C-FA-SF binder combination optimizes workability at 5% SF, optimizes strength and reduces porosity at 10%SF; HPGFC with C-SL-SF binder combination reduce workability, strength and porosity when increasing the rate of using SL to replace C.

articleTitle: Applications of Image Processing Techniques to Determine the Lane for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles are considered a huge human technology foundation for the intelligent vehicle industry. To operate on the road, autonomous vehicles must be equipped with many sensors capable of detecting problems in moving instead of humans. In addition to the control software, many modern technologies and algorithms have been applied today, such as image processing, artificial intelligence, etc. This paper describes a method to build an autonomous vehicle system with real cameras, performing the task of automatic navigation in traffic conditions with lines. Lane detection is essential in determining the center of self-driving vehicles concerning the moving lane.

articleTitle: Introduction to the Soil-Structure Interaction Model to Investigate Vibration of the Pillar in the Industrial Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This article presents a survey and evaluation of the relationship between the foundation and structure vibration of an industrial plant. The study aims to introduce a mechanical model representing the interaction between the foundation and the structure under various impact conditions of the environment and machinery. The paper discusses the factors affecting the vibration response of the ground and describes the types of vibrations that can occur in the foundation, including two horizontal vibrations. The article has a detailed description of measuring work, methods, and signal processing. Based on the study's results, future maintenance decisions can be informed by understanding how the foundation behaves under various circumstances. Finally, the paper provides a new foundational vibration analysis method and proposes future research directions.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Motion of Semisubmersible in Irregular Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research aims to evaluate the motion characteristics of a semisubmersible that is moored in both regular waves and irregular waves. The 6-DOF motion responses and tensions of mooring cables have been investigated using the 3D panel method in Ansys AQWA software. Pierson-Mskowitz wave spectrum has opted for the environmental load acting on the semisubmersible. The results of numerical simulation are verified with those of experiment data in both frequency domain and time domain in regular waves. The motion responses of the semisubmersible and the cable tensions in irregular waves of sea state 5 and sea state 6 are then evaluated.

articleTitle: Identity-Based Authenticated Encryption in Internet of Medical Things
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper introduces an authentication protocol that relies on identity-based authentication to safeguard the medical data system in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). The protocol uses Public-Key algorithms to control access and generate secure session keys. To ensure the confidentiality and integrity of data, both the Counter CBC-MAC Mode and Galois Counter Mode are utilized to perform authenticated encryption protocols. Our proposed protocols are developed based on user identities associated with their secret keys. In the IoMT, authorized users with valid identities can access encrypted medical records. The results demonstrate that our proposed protocols protect against statistical and differential attacks. The computational cost of the secure protocols is also suitable for medical data management systems, as it requires low resource utilization.

articleTitle: Wind Energy Forecasting: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis of machine learning and deep learning techniques for wind energy forecasting. Wind energy prediction is a crucial aspect of renewable energy management. We study and assess the application of tree-based algorithms (LightGBM, CatBoost, and Random Forest) and deep learning approaches (feedforward networks with skip connection and FT-transformers). In the numerical study, we evaluate forecasting accuracy, robustness, computational efficiency, and analyze the reasons why some methods are better than others. This research contributes to advancing wind energy forecasting methodologies in the renewable energy sector. Accurate predictive models play the most crucial role in optimizing wind energy integration into the grid, supporting a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Vehicle Blind Spot Detection and Tracking System Based on Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Car accidents often happen when vehicles change lanes, turn at intersections, back up, or park in a parking lotthat is especially dangerous. Therefore, detecting people in the blind spots of cars is a significant issue. There are many methods to detect people. However, those problems do not completelysolve the problem. To solve the problem, the article proposes a system to recognize people entering the blind spot behind acar. The method that we use is to combine image processing algorithms with microwave radar sensors to collect information about the vehicle's surroundings. We use the Yolo-fastest module to extract human detection through the parts of the human body (arms, legs, head, torso), combined to increase recognition ability. Besides, using microwave radar sensors are used to detect moving objects. The results on cars have achieved 91.63% accuracy and have potential applications in self-driving cars and advanced driver assistance systems.

articleTitle: A Review of the Free-Fall Lifeboat During Its Launching from a Moving Ship
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Free-fall lifeboat (FFLB) launch is necessary for safe marine evacuation, especially for fast leave extreme maritime accidents. This study presents a retrospective review of the FFLB launch by content analysis approaches. The overview and legal foundation of FFLB for evaluating dynamic response criteria is investigated. The classify the existing method for assessment of the dynamic motion of FFLB during launching and after water entry is studied. The effects of skid angle and skid height on the water entry impact of lifeboat design are analyzed and discussed. Skid angle and skid height have a significant effect on the trajectory and the acceleration of the FFLB, it is especially important to determine these influencing parameters, because it can help the FFLB to move away from the hazardous area and reduce the risk of an accident during launch. Further research is needed in the topics of the performance of FFLB during the evacuation process such as examination of the best dropping angle and safe seat orientation for each possible FFLB's launch task under disruptive environmental conditions.

articleTitle: A Simulation and Analysis of the Effect of Temperature Fields and Velocity Fields on Operating Room Standards by Using CFD Software
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Scientific Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this study, the values of temperature and velocity inside the operating room are of interest to analyze and evaluate the design process of buildings that satisfy the set standards and conditions by using Autodesk rendering software and numerical simulation software to build and set initial parameters. The simulation results through analysis show the value of the temperature field with uniform distribution, especially in section 2, with the temperature range from 20 °C to 22 °C satisfying the design criteria for the standard of the operation room. At cross-section 3, the temperature value is reached at the air supply vein with a deal within 15°C in accordance with the original design parameter. For the velocity field results, it is reasonable compared with the parameters of previous studies with the working zone velocity of the doctor and the patient in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.068\ m/s$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15\ m/s$</tex> which is less than the standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5\ m/s$</tex> for the standard requirements of the operating room, With the airflow inside the operating room moving at a slow speed, this helps verify that the design process has satisfied the initial requirements. In addition, the slow-moving air flow will help reduce the risk of spreading the virus to the surrounding environment on medical equipment and instruments, especially by creating a comfortable environment that meets the standards of room surgery. From here, the simulation results obtained are positive and very encouraging to minimize the virus dispersion and establish the comfort zone.
